onet.title: Network and Computer Systems Administrators
onet.description: Install, configure, and maintain an organization's local area network (LAN), wide area network (WAN), data communications network, operating systems, and physical and virtual servers. Perform system monitoring and verify the integrity and availability of hardware, network, and server resources and systems. Review system and application logs and verify completion of scheduled jobs, including system backups. Analyze network and server resource consumption and control user access. Install and upgrade software and maintain software licenses. May assist in network modeling, analysis, planning, and coordination between network and data communications hardware and software.

task.title: Maintain and administer computer networks and related computing environments, including computer hardware, systems software, applications software, and all configurations.
Perform data backups and disaster recovery operations.
Diagnose, troubleshoot, and resolve hardware, software, or other network and system problems, and replace defective components when necessary.
Configure, monitor, and maintain email applications or virus protection software.
Operate master consoles to monitor the performance of computer systems and networks and to coordinate computer network access and use.
Monitor network performance to determine whether adjustments are needed and where changes will be needed in the future.
Plan, coordinate, and implement network security measures to protect data, software, and hardware.
Analyze equipment performance records to determine the need for repair or replacement.
Confer with network users about solutions to existing system problems.
Recommend changes to improve systems and network configurations, and determine hardware or software requirements related to such changes.
Design, configure, and test computer hardware, networking software and operating system software.
Perform routine network startup and shutdown procedures, and maintain control records.
Load computer tapes and disks, and install software and printer paper or forms.
Train people in computer system use.
Maintain logs related to network functions, as well as maintenance and repair records.
Gather data pertaining to customer needs, and use the information to identify, predict, interpret, and evaluate system and network requirements.
Coordinate with vendors and with company personnel to facilitate purchases.
Implement and provide technical support for voice services and equipment, such as private branch exchange, voice mail system, and telecom system.
Maintain an inventory of parts for emergency repairs.
Research new technologies by attending seminars, reading trade articles, or taking classes, and implement or recommend the implementation of new technologies.

activity.title: Maintain computer networks to enhance performance and user access.
Implement security measures for computer or information systems.
Create electronic data backup to prevent loss of information.
Resolve computer network problems.
Resolve computer software problems.
Troubleshoot issues with computer applications or systems.
Monitor the performance of computer networks.
Develop computer or information security policies or procedures.
Analyze data to identify or resolve operational problems.
Provide technical support for computer network issues.
Analyze project data to determine specifications or requirements.
Identify information technology project resource requirements.
Recommend changes to improve computer or information systems.
Collaborate with others to resolve information technology issues.
Design integrated computer systems.
Test computer hardware performance.
Test software performance.
Document operational activities.
Install computer hardware.
Train others in computer interface or software use.
Document network-related activities or tasks.
Collect data about customer needs.
Coordinate resource procurement activities.
Conduct research to gain information about products or processes.
Maintain the inventory of equipment.
Update knowledge about emerging industry or technology trends.

element.name: Selective Attention

element.name: Speech Clarity

element.name: Mathematical Reasoning

element.name: Number Facility

element.name: Perceptual Speed

element.name: Visualization

element.name: Finger Dexterity

element.name: Memorization

element.name: Arm-Hand Steadiness

element.name: Speed of Closure

element.name: Time Sharing
element.description: The ability to shift back and forth between two or more activities or sources of information (such as speech, sounds, touch, or other sources).

element.name: Manual Dexterity

element.name: Auditory Attention
element.description: The ability to focus on a single source of sound in the presence of other distracting sounds.

element.name: Wrist-Finger Speed
element.description: The ability to make fast, simple, repeated movements of the fingers, hands, and wrists.

element.name: Hearing Sensitivity

element.name: Depth Perception
element.description: The ability to judge which of several objects is closer or farther away from you, or to judge the distance between you and an object.

element.name: Extent Flexibility

element.name: Rate Control

element.name: Reaction Time

element.name: Multilimb Coordination

element.name: Response Orientation

element.name: Trunk Strength

element.name: Dynamic Strength
element.description: The ability to exert muscle force repeatedly or continuously over time. This involves muscular endurance and resistance to muscle fatigue.

element.name: Dynamic Flexibility
element.description: The ability to quickly and repeatedly bend, stretch, twist, or reach out with your body, arms, and/or legs.

element.name: Explosive Strength
element.description: The ability to use short bursts of muscle force to propel oneself (as in jumping or sprinting), or to throw an object.

element.name: Glare Sensitivity
element.description: The ability to see objects in the presence of a glare or bright lighting.

element.name: Gross Body Coordination
element.description: The ability to coordinate the movement of your arms, legs, and torso together when the whole body is in motion.

element.name: Gross Body Equilibrium

element.name: Night Vision

element.name: Peripheral Vision

element.name: Sound Localization

element.name: Spatial Orientation

element.name: Speed of Limb Movement

element.name: Stamina

element.name: Static Strength

element.name: Achievement Orientation

element.name: Self-Confidence

element.name: Cooperation

element.name: Sincerity

trades.description: A Network Administrator sets up, monitors, and maintains the computer networks that connect offices, devices, and systems. They install routers and switches, manage user accounts, fix internet or server problems, update security settings, and test backups so data can be recovered. Their work keeps computers, phones, files, and online services running safely and reliably.

A Systems Engineer designs and manages the computer-based systems that help an organization work smoothly. They plan how hardware, software, networks, and data tools fit together, test performance, fix problems, and help upgrades run properly. Their work keeps important technology connected, reliable, and secure for everyday business, communication, and services.
